questions.question: Describe the Khoikhoi way of life and explain why the Mossel Bay area was important to them.
questions.expected_answer: The Khoikhoi were herders who kept fat-tailed sheep and cattle and counted their wealth in animals. They lived in groups led by chiefs and moved with the seasons with portable mat houses to find grazing and water. The Mossel Bay area had good grazing and freshwater springs, which were precious for people and animals, especially in the dry season.

questions.question: Describe what happened at Mossel Bay in February 1488.
questions.expected_answer: On the third of February 1488, Dias anchored in the bay and called it the watering place of Saint Blaise. Needing water, the sailors landed near Khoikhoi herders, who moved their cattle away. The Portuguese began filling barrels at a spring, the Khoikhoi threw stones from a hill to drive them off, and Dias fired a crossbow and killed a Khoikhoi man. It was the first recorded meeting and killing between Europeans and southern Africans.

questions.question: Explain the event from both the Portuguese and Khoikhoi points of view.
questions.expected_answer: The Portuguese were tired, thirsty sailors who saw the water as free, felt attacked by the stones and defended themselves. The Khoikhoi saw strangers arrive without permission and take water from a spring their people and animals depended on in the dry season, without speaking their language or offering anything, so they threw stones to protect their water and cattle, and then one of them was killed.
